newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Guam airport official says 30 survivors in crash.
newsitem.headline: Guam airport official says 30 survivors in crash.

text.p: At least 30 people are believed to have survived the Korean Air Lines Boeing 747 airliner crash in Guam in the early hours of Wednesday, an airport official said.

"We believe there are 29 to 30 survivors and most have been taken to the Navy medical centre," Andrew Murphy, spokesman for the Guam Airport Authority, told Reuters by telephone. Korean Air Lines said there were 254 people on board, including 23 crew members.
Earlier reports of the number of people on board varied from 228 to 331.
Murphy said the Korean Air Lines flight, which originated in Seoul, crashed about seven miles (12 km) south of the airport.
"At about 1.50 in the morning, the control tower received word that a Boeing 747 Korean Air Lines flight has crashed. The report is still sketchy," Murphy said.
He said the aircraft had crashed in a sparsely populated area called Limits.
